# Bike4Mind

> An AI workspace: notebooks (sessions) over many LLM providers, files and data
> lakes, artifacts, and agents. Bike4Mind is open source and self-hostable.

Every path below is root-relative, so resolve it against the origin you fetched
this file from. That keeps the file correct for bike4mind.com and for any
self-hosted deployment.

## Agents

- [The Open Door](/api/agent-quest/manifest): `agent-quest` - an onboarding quest
  built for agents rather than for people. Read the manifest, speak MCP, out-think
  a scheduling puzzle, make something, and sign the Wall of Agents. Completing it
  earns a free credit grant and a verifiable badge. Steps carry a `status`; only
  an `available` step has an `endpoint` to call. Also served over MCP as
  `b4m://agent-quest`.

## Authentication

- Send an API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` on every HTTP API request.
  The `X-API-Key` header is still accepted but is the legacy form.
- Read the key from the environment variable `B4M_API_KEY`. The MCP server reads
  the same variable, plus `B4M_API_URL` for the deployment origin.
- A user creates a key in the web app under Profile > API Keys, at
  `/profile?tab=api-keys`. Ask for the narrowest scopes the task needs.
- Never ask the user to paste a key into a chat, and never print, log, or commit
  one. If `B4M_API_KEY` is unset, tell the user to create a key and export it.
- Some routes are not in the contract yet. If one you need is missing, say so
  rather than guessing its shape.

## Grounded answer

To answer from a data lake's files, the key needs `datalake:read`,
`notebooks:write` and `ai:chat`. Four calls:

1. `GET /api/v1/data-lakes`: pick a lake `id`. Paginated: pass `next_cursor`
   back as `cursor` until it is `null`.
2. `POST /api/v1/sessions` with `{"name", "dataLakeId"}`: keep the response
   `id`. `dataLakeId` already turns on forced retrieval, so do not send
   `forceKnowledgeRetrieval`.
3. `POST /api/chat` with `{"sessionId", "message"}`: read
   `tracking_info.quest_id` from the reply.
4. Poll `GET /api/v1/quests/{quest_id}` while `status` is `pending` or
   `running`; stop at `done` or `stopped`.

- Check for failure before reading the answer: `type: "error"` (with
  `errorCode` when classified) or a `stopped` status is a failed turn. A run
  that died part-way still polls back as `done`, with `promptMeta.finishReason`
  set to `timeout` or `abandoned`: treat that text as partial.
- Read `reply`: the visible answer, with `<think>...</think>` blocks and any
  trailing choices block already removed. It is `null` only while the turn
  has not written anything yet (`pending`/`running`). `replies[]` is the raw
  stored slots; you do not need it.
- Polling does not use the daily key quota.
- Request and response shapes: the [API reference](/api/v1/docs).

## API

- [OpenAPI contract](/api/v1/openapi.json): the machine-readable HTTP API. Served
  with the current deployment as its `servers` entry, so it is ready for SDK
  codegen.
- [Deployment OpenAPI contract](/api/v1/openapi.deployment.json): the contract
  above plus the endpoints of any add-on packages this deployment mounts. Identical
  to it when there are none.
- [API reference](/api/v1/docs): the same contract, rendered for reading.

## MCP

Bike4Mind ships its own MCP server over stdio or loopback HTTP:

```
npx -y @bike4mind/cli@latest mcp serve
```

It exposes the Bike4Mind tools plus the resources `b4m://notebook/{id}`,
`b4m://file/{id}`, `b4m://project/{id}`, `b4m://artifact/{id}`, and
`b4m://agent-quest`. Every resource except `b4m://agent-quest` needs
credentials; the quest manifest is deliberately readable without them.
